result.title: Average-Reward Policy Identification from a Single Continuing Trajectory
result.summary: In reinforcement learning, an agent must explore an unknown environment to learn how to make good decisions. Unlike methods that can freely sample any state--action pair, an agent learning from a single trajectory must spend additional time navigating between states. It is therefore natural to expect that learning from a single trajectory requires more experience. In this paper, we show that this additional cost is not always necessary. For average-reward reinforcement learning, we develop an algorithm that learns where to collect information while ensuring that the required samples can be obtained efficiently. We establish an upper bound on the number of interactions needed to identify a near-optimal policy. Furthermore, we prove a matching information theoretic lower bound, showing that, for a broad class of environments and at sufficiently high accuracy, learning from a single trajectory is no harder in the worst case than learning with unrestricted access to state action samples. Our results reveal that the additional complexity cost of navigation can be avoided by adapting information gathering requirements to how the environment provides information.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究平均奖励强化学习中仅凭单条持续轨迹学习近最优策略的问题，提出一种自适应安排「在哪里收集信息」的算法，给出交互次数上界并证明匹配的信息论下界，说明在最坏情况下单轨迹学习并不比无限制采样更难。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按环境提供信息的方式调整信息收集需求」的思路，或可类比 LVR 中何时、何处获取视觉证据与动态计算、停止决策的成本权衡，线索较远，可供核查但需较多迁移。
